questions: Do the outer sensors at x = ±0.06 m still read the tape well at 16 mm, or do readings saturate or drop out between the 0.02 m pitch sensors?
Is line loss gone? If not, at what error does it begin: at the outer sensors or during the first steps from the start?
Does sensor y = 0.03 m reduce steering oscillation on the slalom compared with iteration 0, or does the earlier reaction cause overshoot?
If the robot now stays on track but does not complete, is speed the limit? Would you test wheel_radius 0.035 m and mass 0.7 kg next?

intent: Test whether a wider, seven-sensor, larger-footprint array that sits closer to the axle stops line loss and keeps the robot inside the 0.06 m off-track limit. The change is aimed at the failure seen in iteration 0, where max_error reached the limit as the line left the array. Expected result: line_loss_events near 0, max_error under 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and the first completions on the oval.
learning: Iteration 0 showed that all trials ended off track at about 0.062 m max error with about one line-loss event each. The sensing span (about ±0.058 m) is too narrow for the off-track limit. This iteration widens the span to ±0.06 m with 16 mm footprints. Next, check whether line loss stops and whether max_error falls under 0.06 m. If line loss stops but the robot still leaves the track, the controller gain is the limit, not geometry. If it completes, then speed becomes the next geometry lever.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with zero completions. Every run ended off track, not by stall. Max error was about 0.062 m on all three tracks, just over the 0.06 m off-track floor. Body width cannot help: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4), which stays at 0.06 for any allowed body width up to 0.18 m. The robot is therefore leaving the track because of its tracking error. Each run also logged about one line-loss event, which points at the sensing array. With the baseline five sensors at 0.02 m pitch, the outer sensors reach only about 0.058 m of lateral offset before the tape leaves the array. The robot loses the line at roughly the same offset where it leaves the track, so the array has no margin to recover. Changes: (1) widen the array to 7 sensors spanning x = ±0.06 m at 0.02 m pitch, so the line stays visible out to about 0.07 m of offset; (2) enlarge the footprint to 16 mm, which widens each sensor's pickup and keeps adjacent readings overlapping; (3) move the sensor row from y = 0.04 to y = 0.03 m, closer to the axle, as the Integrator suggested for smoother reactions, while keeping it ahead of the wheels. Track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m and mass 0.8 kg are unchanged, so any change in result is attributable to sensing. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0, max_error drops below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend, and at least some runs complete. Weights for the Integrator should be roughly proportional to x (about ±2 at the outer sensors), and the signal scale should be checked.
